title: Nox & Pico — « Elle t’éclaire. Nuance. » (sketch IA, début de l’épisode 1)

setups.framing: Medium single of Pico, frontal, eye level, waist up (approved image, used as is)
setups.description: The approved image pico_ref.png, unchanged, is the start image. Camera inside the workshop on Nox's side of the bench (his point of view), about 2.5 m from the door, at standing eye height. Pico has just stopped in the open doorway, centred, facing the lens; her left forearm is raised across her chest with the smartwatch toward the camera, brows frowned, mouth closed. Behind her: the dark brick hallway, a metal shelf with books and a small green LED string, a pendant lamp top right; the grey door leaf stands open at screen-left; dark workshop wall in the left foreground. Used for shot 1 only, and for the first voice test.

setups.framing: Close-up of Nox soldering, low angle from bench level, three-quarter front
setups.description: Camera resting on the workbench top on Nox's right-hand side (the soldering-station side), about 40 cm from his hands, tilted up about 25 degrees at his face, which is bowed over his work; his body is turned three-quarters toward screen-right. Bottom of the frame: his right hand holding the soldering iron (blue handle), its tip on a small circuit board, a thin wisp of smoke. His face fills the upper two-thirds: eyes lowered behind the green-tinted glasses, mouth closed, rebel lock of hair. Because the camera is low, the bowed face is seen almost frontally: the mouth must be fully visible and above the bottom fifth of the frame (caption zone). Behind and above him: dark bookshelves, the string of round green bulbs, the glow of one CRT monitor, a slice of the night window at the right edge. Nobody else in frame. If the soldering stand is visible it must be EMPTY (the iron is in his hand; nox_ref shows it in its stand, and two irons must not appear). Reference: nox_ref for the character and the set. Used for shots 2 and 7. Common to every new still: same flat-shaded, clean-outline cutscene rendering, palette and night lighting as the two approved images; 4:3; no text, letters or numbers anywhere (screens and pinned notes show abstract shapes); Pico: red high ponytail with GREEN elastic, long strands round the face, yellow sweatshirt, black headphones round her neck, black smartwatch on her LEFT wrist; Nox: blue-black spiky hair with a rebel lock, thin green-tinted glasses, black turtleneck, anthracite bomber with green zip trim, earbud in his LEFT ear; screen direction for the whole film: Nox on the left looking right, Pico on the right looking left (the camera never crosses to the window side of the Nox-door axis: it stays on that axis or on Nox's right-hand side). Ask for it as a NEW camera angle with the approved images as image_references, never as a copy of them.

setups.framing: Side-on two-shot across the workbench, waist up, at the eye level of the seated Nox
setups.description: The only frame with both faces. Camera perpendicular to the Nox-door axis, on Nox's right-hand side of the room (opposite the window), about 2.5 m from the bench, lens at the eye height of the seated Nox (about 1.15 m), normal lens, everything in focus. Screen-left: Nox seated behind his bench, right profile facing screen-right, still bent over his circuit board with the soldering iron in his right hand, eyes on his work, mouth closed. Screen-right: Pico on the visitor side, bent forward over the bench, right forearm planted flat on the bench top among his components, left elbow propped on the bench and left forearm reaching across so that the watch sits about 15 cm in front of his glasses, between his face and the board. She stares at him, one eyebrow raised, lips firmly closed (left profile). Background between them: the tall night window with city lights, the string of green bulbs along the top, bookshelves and a CRT monitor behind Nox; at the far right edge, a slice of the grey door frame and dark brick. The bench top crosses the lower third (grey mug on the far side, empty soldering stand in the foreground). Both faces and the watch stay above the bottom fifth of the frame (caption zone). References: nox_ref and pico_ref. Used for shots 3 and 6. Eyes narrowed in a sceptical squint, fixed on the watch. Background dark and simple (brick, a hint of the door frame). The bench surface fills the bottom fifth of the frame (caption zone). shots.speaker: pico
shots.text: Nox ! Pourquoi ma montre fait des lumières vertes à la fin de mon run ?
shots.caption: Nox ! Pourquoi ma montre fait des lumières vertes à la fin de mon run ?
shots.acting: Breathless, she has just skidded to a stop; no hello. "Nox !" sharp, then the question in one breath, fast and pressing, very intrigued. One beat: she shakes her raised watch wrist toward him once on "ma montre", eyes locked on him (the lens). After the last word she holds the wrist out and the stare, mouth closed.
shots.listener: Nox is off-screen (the camera is his point of view).
shots.camera: Locked. The clip opens on the posed still, door already open.
shots.sfx: Door bang on the first frame; a short sneaker squeak under it (optional).
shots.notes: The caption of the question is on screen from 0.1 s: it is the hook. Longest line (15 words): frontal, medium size, one mouth. "run" is the English word as French runners say it. A faint green flicker under the watch case is welcome but must not be forced. First voice test: this clip needs no new still.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.caption: Bonsoir à toi aussi, Pico.
shots.acting: First sentence of l02. He does not flinch: he keeps soldering through one silent second, eyes down. Then he says it to his circuit board without looking up: dry, sing-song, mock-offended, a smile in the voice, brisk (alive, never slow). One beat: a single eyebrow lifts on "aussi"; his eyes never leave the solder joint.
shots.listener: Pico is off-screen; her sneaker steps cross the room under the silent second (added in the edit).
shots.sfx: Faint soldering sizzle; Pico's quick steps approaching during the silent second.
shots.notes: The silent second before the deadpan answer is the first laugh (as reference 2, shot 11). If the model starts speaking at once, hold the opening frames in the edit. Safety take on this same still: the whole of l02 in one clip (about 4.2 s), which replaces shots 2 and 3 if the two-shot fails.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.caption: Entre, fais comme chez toi.
shots.acting: Second sentence of l02. The hard cut reveals that she is already sprawled on his bench with the watch under his nose: the laugh is on the cut. He stays bent over his work; one beat: he lifts his head a few centimetres, just enough to look at her over the watch. Warm, amused sarcasm, an old habit between them, quick.
shots.listener: Pico frozen, wrist held 15 cm from his glasses, staring at him, eyebrow raised, lips closed. Her stillness is the joke.
shots.camera: Locked. Half a second on the tableau before the line, so that the reveal reads.
shots.notes: The only speaking shot with two visible faces: the prompt names the speaker (the young man on the left) and says the girl on the right keeps her lips closed and does not move. Short line (6 syllables), in profile. If her lips move anyway: remake the still with her head turned further from the camera. If the still itself fails: use the safety take of shot 2 and drop shots 3 and 6.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.text: Tu portes cette montre depuis deux ans… et tu découvres qu'elle s'allume ?
shots.caption: Tu portes cette montre depuis deux ans… et tu découvres qu’elle s’allume ?
shots.acting: Kept whole so that the pause plays in real time. Teasing, deadpan-playful, quick, a smile in the voice. His eyes are on the watch for "Tu portes cette montre depuis deux ans…"; one beat: on the "…" he looks up at her face with one raised eyebrow and a corner smile, then finishes the question lightly, enjoying it.
shots.listener: Pico's shoulder and forearm in the foreground do not move.
shots.camera: Locked. The one shot above 4 s.
shots.notes: 13 words on a three-quarter face of medium size, never on a close-up, so that a lip-sync slip shows least. The "…" is a short held pause, not a slowdown. Spare take: the same line on nox_face (made anyway as part of the first voice test).

shots.speaker: pico
shots.caption: J’ai jamais regardé dessous, ok ?
shots.acting: Caught out: a blank, frozen stare for the short silence, then the line fast, stung and defensive, a bit sulky. One beat: on "ok ?" she lifts her chin, pouts and looks away to screen-right; she holds the pout.
shots.notes: First use of the Pico close-up. Listen for the word "ok".

shots.speaker: none
shots.acting: Silent stand-off, nobody speaks. Exactly the tableau of shot 3: he has already gone back to his soldering and does not look at her; she is still planted on his bench, wrist under his nose, glaring at him. Only the wisp of smoke moves.
shots.listener: Both hold perfectly still, lips closed.
shots.camera: Locked. Same still as shot 3 (reference 1 also reuses its wide before and after the gag).
shots.sfx: Soldering sizzle and room tone only; the clip's own sound is muted.
shots.notes: The silent beat before his answer, played with both characters in frame. Cheapest way: one silent clip from the same still (nobody speaks, nobody moves, only the smoke), or failing that the still itself held for 1.3 s. Removable without any other change: shot 5 then cuts straight to shot 7.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.caption: Bon. Laisse-moi t’expliquer.
shots.acting: Still soldering, eyes down: a short amused breath out through the nose, then "Bon." to his board. One beat: he lifts his head from his work toward her (screen-right) while his iron hand sinks out of the bottom of the frame, for a brisk, warm, eager "Laisse-moi t'expliquer." (he loves explaining; alive, never slow).
shots.camera: Locked, low angle. Same still as shot 2.
shots.notes: The sigh is a breath, not a word: reject any take with an added word. The iron leaves the frame here because it is back in its stand in shot 8.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.caption: Regarde de plus près.
shots.acting: First sentence of l03, his catchphrase. One beat: he pushes his glasses up with one index finger and a green glint slides across the lenses; then the line, low, playful, conspiratorial, an invitation (alive, not slow). The hand drops back out of frame.
shots.listener: Pico is off-screen (the camera is her point of view).
shots.sfx: A tiny glint sound on the glasses (optional).
shots.notes: His signature before every revelation. It is the only shot where a hand enters the frame, next to thin glasses: also make a take without the hand (he leans a little toward the lens, green glint only) and choose in the edit. Ask for a perfectly still background with frozen screens. Five syllables in a 5 s clip: check that no word is added.

shots.speaker: nox
shots.text: Ta montre envoie de la lumière verte… dans ta peau.
shots.caption: Ta montre envoie de la lumière verte… dans ta peau.
shots.acting: Second sentence of l03, spoken OFF-SCREEN by Nox. Lively storyteller relish, close and captivating; a short suspense pause after "verte…", then "dans ta peau." in a mock-mysterious near-whisper. Never slow.
shots.listener: Pico is on screen and has taken "look closer" literally: eyes 10 cm from the watch, squinting, green light pulsing on her skin. One beat: on "dans ta peau" her eyes go wide and flick up to him. Her mouth stays hidden behind her forearm, which does not move.
shots.sfx: A soft, low electronic pulse in time with the green light (optional).
shots.notes: The image of the sketch: the green light on her skin, the subject of the episode, shown rather than told. Off-screen line, as in reference 1, shot 2: the model may give the voice to the girl, change the voice or stay silent. Safety take: the same sentence on ots_nox with Nox on screen (eyes on the watch, then up to her on "dans ta peau"); its sound can be laid over this picture, where no mouth is visible, or the take can replace the shot.

shots.speaker: pico
shots.caption: Attends… quoi ?! Elle me scanne ?!
shots.acting: Her signature double-take. "Attends…" low and frozen, eyes dropping toward her wrist (below the frame); one beat: her head jerks back and her eyes snap up to Nox, wide, on "quoi ?!", then "Elle me scanne ?!" loud, rising, a touch of panic. She holds the shocked face after the last word.
shots.notes: The line stays whole in one clip: split in two it would give two clips of 3 syllables that the model pads with invented words, and two voices for one outcry. Same still as shot 5, but her previous appearance is the eyes-over-watch shot, so the framing is not repeated twice in a row. Listen for the word "scanne".

shots.speaker: nox
shots.caption: Elle t’éclaire. Nuance.
shots.acting: A silent deadpan stare for 1.2 s, with one slow blink. Then dry, precise, quick and amused: "Elle t'éclaire.", a micro-pause, "Nuance." tossed off. One beat: the corner of his mouth lifts after "Nuance."; he holds the smirk 0.7 s to the final cut. Deadpan in the face, alive in the voice.
shots.camera: Slow push-in of about 12-15% over the whole shot, the only camera move of the film. Generate the clip locked and do the push-in in the edit; plan B is to ask the model for a very slow push-in.
shots.sfx: None: the music bed stops on the cut into this shot, so that the stare and the line play over silence.
shots.notes: Punchline and end of the film (as the last shot of reference 1: silent stare, line, faint smirk). The approved direction says "très posé": that is played in the face and in the pause, not in a slow voice, which makes him robotic.

music: A discreet, slow lo-fi loop (soft bass, no lead melody, no vocals), mixed about 16 dB under the voices, entering just after the door bang and cut dead on the cut into shot 11 so that the stare and the punchline play over silence.
open_questions: Voice: does an audio reference make the character speak in that exact voice, and how good is the French? First batch of 8 jobs before anything else, using only the two approved images: l01 on pico_porte and l02b on nox_face, each on seedance_2_0 and on seedance_2_5 (mode omni_reference), with and without the character's voice sample. Judge timbre, French, lip-sync, and the words "Nox", "run" and "deux ans".
Voice samples: are there clean 8-15 s recordings, without music, of the two validated voices (Nox: Umbriel, Pico: Laomedeia)? seedance_2_0 only takes audio references of 2-15 s.
If the voices still drift from clip to clip, is a voice-change pass after generation acceptable (same timing, so the lips still match)?
Shot 9 has an off-screen voice: will the model produce Nox's voice when no mouth is in frame? If not, the edit lays the sound of the safety take (same sentence on ots_nox) over the picture.

montage.py only trims clips. Holding the opening frames (silent beats of shots 2 and 11), the push-in of shot 11, muting shot 6 and laying another take's sound over shot 9 need small ffmpeg pre-steps or new options.

Is a seventh new image allowed? It would buy an alternative shot 10: the side two-shot again, with Pico recoiled, arm outstretched, and Nox sipping his coffee, the mug hiding his mouth (from the comedy-first proposal).
Length: 31.8 s estimated from syllable counts (expect 30-35 s with generated speech). If the cut lands under 30 s, lengthen the silent beats of shots 2, 6 and 11 rather than add a shot?
The room will not match perfectly from one angle to the next (it does not in reference 2 either): acceptable as long as the characters, the props and the screen direction hold?
Captions: white with a dark outline, the whole line at the bottom (reference 1, and what montage.py does now), with "ok" kept in lower case as in the approved text?
